UPSTREAM: drm/amdgpu: refine SR-IOV firmware VRAM reservation to protect data The previous solution will create a zero buffer on the system domain and then move the zeroes to the VRAM. This will break the original data on the VRAM. Refine the code to create bo on VRAM domain directly and then remove and re-create mem node to the exact position before bo_pin. This can avoid breaking the data and will not cause eviction. UPSTREAM: PCI: Add pci_resize_resource() for resizing BARs Add a pci_resize_resource() interface to allow device drivers to resize BARs of their devices. This is useful for devices with large local storage, e.g., graphics devices. These devices often only expose 256MB BARs initially to be compatible with 32-bit systems. This function only tries to reprogram the windows of the bridge directly above the requesting device and only the BAR of the same type (usually mem, 64bit, prefetchable). This is done to avoid disturbing other drivers by changing the BARs of their devices. Drivers should use the following sequence to resize their BARs: 1. Disable memory decoding of the device using the PCI cfg dword. 2. Use pci_release_resource() to release all BARs which can move during the resize, including the one you want to resize. 3. Call pci_resize_resource() for each BAR you want to resize. 4. Call pci_assign_unassigned_bus_resources() to reassign new locations for all BARs which are not resized, but could move. 5. If everything worked as expected, enable memory decoding in the device again using the PCI cfg dword. BUG=b:79158447 TEST=boot Grunt, run graphics_SanAngeles and login_LoginSuccess Signed-off-by: Christian Knig <christian.koenig@amd.com> Signed-off-by: Bjorn Helgaas <bhelgaas@google.com> (cherry picked from commit 8bb705e3e79d84e77edd4499e74483dd96a4626c) Signed-off-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Change-Id: I7bdd3bced12824a64d2c56512b278f39b3120780 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1123581 Commit-Ready: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Tested-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/amd/amdgpu: fix UVD mc offsets When UVD bo is created, its size is based on the information from firmware header (ucode_size_bytes). The same value should be be used when programming UVD mc controller offsets, otherwise it can happen that (mmUVD_VCPU_CACHE_OFFSET2 + mmUVD_VCPU_CACHE_SIZE2) will point AMDGPU_GPU_PAGE_SIZE bytes after the UVD bo end. Second issue is that when programming the mmUVD_VCPU_CACHE_SIZE0 register, AMDGPU_UVD_FIRMWARE_OFFSET should be taken into account. If it isn't, (mmUVD_VCPU_CACHE_OFFSET2 + mmUVD_VCPU_CACHE_SIZE2) will always point AMDGPU_UVD_FIRMWARE_OFFSET bytes after the UVD bo end. v2: move firmware size calculation into macro definition v3: align firmware size to the gpu page size BUG=b:79158447 TEST=boot Grunt, run graphics_SanAngeles and login_LoginSuccess Reviewed-by: Christian Knig <christian.koenig@amd.com> Signed-off-by: Piotr Redlewski <predlewski@gmail.com> Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com> (cherry picked from commit c1fe75c9e42c8c598a7fb810ecc4f7be258e700c) Signed-off-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Change-Id: Ib1aae6518f71d857e98c3a4301373f1ba9ae098a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1123606 Commit-Ready: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Tested-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

Allow experimentation for Instant Tethering on Eve. Remove default Instant Tethering support on Eve. This is not intended to actually turn off Instant Tethering for Eve, but rather will allow the Bluetooth team to run experiments with Instant Tethering on or off. This change is targeting M69, and will also need to be cherrypicked into M68. It will likely be reverted in M70. apk-cache: Clean up apk-cache-cleaner-jailed's minijail0 invocation This change: * Cleans up the minijail0 invocation for apk-cache-cleaner. * Does not try to invoke the cleaner unless the .apk cache directory exists. This should avoid asserts on systems where the directory has not been created (i.e. systems where ARC has never been enabled before).
